title: Does anyone tried making stock trading bots with astra codex?
author: dhruvhat
selftext: As the title says, what was your experience and was it fruitful?

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
Built a few with coding agents, not that one specifically. The bot is the easy part now, you get a runnable loop in an afternoon. Where it went wrong every time was the backtest, not the bot: the agent used the signal bar's close and filled at that same bar's open, or computed an indicator over the whole series and then sliced it. Both look amazing on a chart.

Two things helped. Tell it a fill may only use bars strictly before the fill bar, and make it print the timestamps it used for each trade. Then run it on paper for a few weeks and compare with what the backtest claims those same weeks should have been. If they disagree, the bot is fine and the test is lying. Daily bars or intraday?

replies.author: dhruvhat
replies.body: Are you already running the bots?

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: Yes, on paper only, since late August. Some are green, some are red, and the number I actually watch is the gap between what the backtest promised for those weeks and what the paper fills came in at. When they agree I trust the test a bit more. When they don't, the test was lying, not the bot.

replies.author: dhruvhat
replies.body: Have you also implemented news and sentiments?

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: No, price and volume only so far. I tried headline scoring once and the problem was the data, not the model: the historical feed had sentiment stamped after the fact, and article timestamps drifted from when they actually hit the wire. Lookahead through the data instead of the code. Which news source are you looking at?

replies.author: dhruvhat
replies.body: I am planning to build it, right now my usage is 0% so asking from those who have already got it done and running, I am thinking to have first swing trade bot, rather intra day, intra day requires lots of algorithmic changes,

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: Swing on daily bars is the right first bot. A slow loop lets you eyeball every signal before you trust the code. Two things bit me early: overnight gaps blow straight through stops sized on close to close ranges, and signal to order lag matters far less than you fear. Log each signal with the close it fired on and the fill you got, then compare.
